lead.headline: Europe hands heavy industry more free carbon permits as COP31 enters its final week
lead.dek: Brussels agreed to soften carbon costs for energy-intensive plants through 2030. The price signal that capture, storage and removal projects lean on just got weaker, and taxpayers may be asked to fill the gap.
body: On November 12, EU governments and the European Parliament reached a provisional deal to raise free carbon allowances for industrial installations whose allocation is set by the ETS heat and fuel benchmarks, covering 2026 to 2030. The deal provides a cushion of roughly 121 million free allowances for sectors judged at risk of carbon leakage, above the Commission's original proposal of about 88 million.

The market had been firm going in. The December 2026 EU allowance contract closed at €90.5 a tonne on November 2, its highest since January. The longer view is softer: IEEFA reported on November 11 that ABN AMRO cut its 2030 EU carbon price forecast by 37% in under a year, and argued that a weaker carbon price shifts the cost of industrial decarbonization from polluters to public budgets.

Negotiations are not finished. Ireland, which chairs the Council, circulated a compromise that would slow the phase-out of free permits and exempt smaller installations from new decarbonization requirements. The Commission's July 17 ETS review also proposes bringing 250 million tonnes of permanent domestic removals, from bioenergy with CCS and direct air capture, into the system between 2031 and 2040.

nexus.electrons: Power generators are not the target of this deal. It covers industrial installations whose free allowances depend on heat and fuel use, so electricity's carbon cost stays tied to the market price.
nexus.molecules: Plants that burn fuel for process heat, such as paper and other energy-intensive producers, get lower compliance bills through 2030. Less cost pressure means less urgency to switch fuels or electrify heat.
nexus.pore: Capture and storage projects compete with the price of an allowance. A lower or less certain price weakens the business case, while the proposed 250 million tonne removals channel after 2031 is the clearest long-run demand signal for European storage.
nexus.water: Carbon capture is thirsty. A European Commission JRC assessment found that adding CO2 capture raises a plant's water use per unit of power by 50% to 62% for coal and gas combined cycle plants. Storage has its own water story: pulling brine out of a storage formation frees space for CO2, turning a disposal cost into a treatment opportunity.

use.text: Treat EU carbon price forecasts as policy exposed. Run any CCS, removals or industrial decarbonization model at a lower allowance price as well as the current one.
Watch whether the final text ties free allowances to real decarbonization investment. A November 5 draft reported by MLex would let companies keep most of them even without it.
If your site is allocated on heat or fuel benchmarks, your 2026 to 2030 free allocation is likely to rise. Confirm with your national authority once the text is final.
Removal developers should read the 250 million tonne purchasing proposal closely. A compliance buyer is worth more than any voluntary offtake.

briefs.headline: A year after Texas took over carbon storage permits, the queue is the story
briefs.text: EPA approved the Railroad Commission of Texas as the Class VI permitting authority on November 12, 2025, making Texas the sixth state with primacy. At the time, more than 60 Class VI applications were pending in Texas, about 24% of EPA's national backlog. Louisiana, the first large primacy state, had issued one permit since 2023 and its governor paused new reviews in October 2025. Carbon Pulse has since reported that new Texas applications have slowed and that long-term liability is still unsettled.

use.text: Permit timing is now a state by state variable. Price Gulf Coast storage on Texas timelines, not EPA's.
Pore space leases are long contracts. Ask who holds liability after injection stops before you sign.

briefs.headline: 45Q survived the tax bill. The fight now is over who checks the tonnes
briefs.text: The 45Q credit pays $85 per tonne of CO2 captured at a facility and $180 for direct air capture, and the 2025 tax law set equal values across storage and use. Treasury's Notice 2026-50, issued August 14, extended the safe harbor that lets companies report stored volumes while EPA's reporting rules are in flux. IEEFA argued on October 22 that the change makes claims harder to verify. GAO counted 33 US carbon capture facilities as of March 2026 and found 45Q claims more than tripled from 2019 to 2023.

use.text: The credit value is intact. The risk to model is verification and recapture, not repeal.
PwC advises checking you can meet the independent certification requirement by the time you file.

briefs.headline: Canada's biggest carbon capture bet hit its signing deadline
briefs.text: Ottawa, Alberta and the five Oil Sands Alliance producers set November 15 as the target for binding agreements on the Pathways CCS project, which aims to capture about 6 million tonnes a year by 2035 and 16 million by 2045. Ottawa has committed to extend investment tax credits of 50% on capture equipment and 37.5% on transport and storage. Alberta unveiled lower royalties on some new oil sands output on November 13. A Cenovus executive called the timeline tight on November 4. We found no public confirmation of signed agreements as of this morning. The alliance targets a final investment decision in late 2027 or early 2028.

use.text: Canadian Natural says its 2027 spending plan depends on these agreements. Expect producer guidance to move with them.
Pre-FID engineering for the capture sites and the shared CO2 pipeline is the contract flow to watch in 2027.

briefs.headline: At COP31, governments start acting like carbon removal buyers
briefs.text: COP31 runs in Antalya through November 20, with Türkiye holding the presidency and Australia leading negotiations. On November 11, fifteen countries released a statement on policies to scale carbon credit markets, while delegates split over when credits should be authorized under Article 6. The same day, a Canadian official said the government would announce competitive standing offers for carbon removal in the coming days, part of a plan to buy at least C$10 million of durable removals from direct air capture, bioenergy with CCS and enhanced mineralization.

use.text: Government procurement is small in dollars and large in signal. A standing offer is a reference price you can show lenders.
Article 6 authorization timing decides whether a credit can count toward a country's target. Ask sellers which status yours carries.

briefs.headline: The carbon business is becoming a water business
briefs.text: Capture6 opened Project Tortuga near Perth on October 12: eight containerised units that recover freshwater from brine and capture CO2 from the air, funded under Australia's Carbon Capture Technologies Program. The company estimates that treating Australia's brine could yield up to 470 gigalitres of extra freshwater a year. It is also building Project Monarch for California's Palmdale Water District, due to start operating in the second quarter of 2027. Separately, a KAUST led team reported in Nature that recirculating groundwater lets CO2 be turned to stone in basalt without the large freshwater volumes once assumed; 70% of 131 tons injected in western Saudi Arabia mineralized within ten months.

use.text: Projects that sell both water and carbon removal have two revenue lines. Ask which one carries the economics.
Brine you pay to dispose of is feedstock for these models. Produced water and storage brine are the supply to watch.

briefs.headline: Northern Lights moves its second phase into fabrication
briefs.text: Worley Rosenberg won a Subsea7 contract on October 16 to fabricate subsea structures and spools for Northern Lights Phase II, which expands Norway's open-access CO2 transport and storage network to more than 5 million tonnes a year by 2028. Phase II is the clearest test of whether third-party storage can be sold like pipeline capacity to emitters across Europe.

use.text: European emitters without their own storage can plan around shipped CO2 to Norway on a 2028 horizon.
Open-access storage tariffs are the number to track. They set the floor cost of a stored tonne in Europe.

social.headline: Europe eases carbon costs for heavy industry
social.watch: UK and EU summit on carbon market linkage, Nov 20.
social.caption:
EU governments and Parliament agreed on Nov 12 to give energy-intensive industry roughly 121 million more free carbon permits through 2030. Allowances traded near €90 a tonne, but a softer long-run price weakens the case for carbon capture and shifts cost to taxpayers.

What it means for investors, regulators and industry at carbonenergynexus.com

midday.watch: Final Treasury rules on how stored tonnes are verified.
midday.caption:
The US 45Q credit pays $85 per tonne of captured CO2 and $180 for direct air capture. Treasury extended a reporting safe harbor in August; IEEFA says that makes claims harder to verify. The credit is safe. Verification is the risk.

evening.headline: Canada steps up as a carbon removal buyer
evening.watch: Whether other governments copy standing offers for removals.
evening.caption:
At COP31, Canada said it will announce standing offers to buy carbon removal, part of a C$10 million plan covering direct air capture, bioenergy with CCS and mineralization. Fifteen countries also backed policies to scale carbon credit markets.

minerals.intro: The metals behind grids, batteries, magnets and reactors. Supply sits in a few countries, so policy moves prices as much as demand does, and every mine and refinery is also a water and power project.

items.name: Rare earths
items.headline: China buys two more months on its widest export controls
items.text: Beijing extended its pause on the October 2025 controls to Jan 10, 2027, a day before it lapsed. Licensing on seven medium and heavy rare earths, including dysprosium and terbium, stays in force, and North American oxide prices have climbed. On Nov 6, neodymium metal was quoted at $145 to $157 a kg FOB.

items.name: Copper
items.headline: The AI metal takes a breather
items.text: US copper fell to $6.20 a pound in November, a four month low, as traders reconsidered how fast data center and electrification demand will grow. It set a record of $6.85 in September.

items.name: Lithium
items.headline: Prices near a one year low as a new hedge arrives
items.text: Lithium carbonate in China fell below 95,000 yuan a tonne in November on softer demand and rising supply. The Guangzhou Futures Exchange opens lithium hydroxide futures on Nov 26, giving producers and cathode makers a new way to hedge.

items.name: Cobalt
items.headline: Congo keeps its hand on the tap
items.text: The DRC caps cobalt exports at 96,600 tonnes a year for 2026 and 2027, about half of what it shipped in 2024 by Argus estimates. Its regulator said in August it will hold the quotas and may cut them if the market needs rebalancing.

items.name: Uranium
items.headline: Utilities pay up for fuel years ahead
items.text: TradeTech's long term uranium price reached $99 a pound on Oct 31, the highest since the series began in 1996. US futures traded above $91 in November, the highest since February, on a stronger outlook for nuclear power.

items.name: Minerals policy
items.headline: Washington signs deals faster than mines can open
items.text: The US has signed more than 40 mineral pacts in the current administration, and related investment hit a record $3.2 billion in the second quarter. The agreements lack binding legal force, so projects still need buyers, permits and finance.

innovation.name: Battery style direct air capture
innovation.text: Researchers pulled CO2 from air with an electrochemical cell powered by electricity instead of heat, and showed it working in the lab and at scale with licensee RepAir. Published in Nature Energy.

innovation.name: Batteries that run on captured CO2
innovation.text: Chemists are testing batteries that store energy while capturing CO2 and converting it to carbon monoxide, a chemical feedstock, if wired directly to industrial emitters.

innovation.name: Enhanced geothermal goes commercial
innovation.text: Fervo's first 33 MW GeoBlock at Cape Station in Utah reached commercial operation a day early, built in 23 months. It is the first greenfield enhanced geothermal plant to earn revenue.

innovation.name: Sodium ion grid storage
innovation.text: CATL launched TENER Sodium, a lithium free storage system, and expects 1 GWh of cumulative shipments by the end of 2026 with international deliveries from June 2027.
